title: Test that a dead process releases the ID lock
lead: A test proves that the store lock (`.adj.lock`) is released when the process holding it dies, on unix (flock) and Windows (LockFileEx), as the docs claim.
findings_note: S36 and S37 reviews (2026-10-18), formerly in S40
boundary: **Not in this slice:** changing the lock; network file systems; the userconfig lock beyond reusing the same helper if it is free.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: AGENTS.md and PROJECT.md say the lock "is released when the call returns or the process dies" (C114, S36), and recovery from a crashed `adj ask` depends on it, but no test covers the death case on either platform (S36 and S37 review notes on the retired S40).

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: - `internal/store/lock_death_test.go` (new, built on unix and Windows; skipped elsewhere with a reason).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- The test re-executes its own binary (`os.Args[0]`, `-test.run` for a helper test, an environment variable selecting the helper role) as a child that takes the store lock in a temp store and prints a ready line; the parent waits for it, confirms a second `acquire` with a short timeout fails while the child lives, kills the child (`Process.Kill`), waits for it, then confirms `acquire` succeeds within the timeout and the lock file is still there.
- Mutation-check: with the child alive the second acquire must fail (otherwise the test proves nothing).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: 1. Write the test; there should be no production change. If it fails, stop and report: that is a lock bug, not a test to adjust.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `. scripts/env.sh; go test ./internal/store/...` passes; `GOOS=windows go vet ./...` clean; the Windows CI job runs it; `slicer check --json` clean.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Worktree `.worktrees/<id>` on its own branch. Commit on that branch after `VERDICT: PASS`; no push, no merge, no AI attribution.
